ateChocolate.steps[0].title: Step 1: Remove All Chocolate Immediately
ateChocolate.steps[0].content: Cats are naturally curious but also more sensitive to toxins. Remove any remaining chocolate from their environment.
ateChocolate.steps[1].title: Step 2: Call Poison Control or Vet
ateChocolate.steps[1].content: 📞 ASPCA Poison Control: (888) 426-4435. Cats are more sensitive to theobromine than dogs — small amounts are concerning.
ateChocolate.steps[2].title: Step 3: Do NOT Induce Vomiting Without Vet Approval
ateChocolate.steps[2].content: ⚠️ Cats may hide symptoms until severe. Inducing vomiting risks aspiration. Only do so if instructed by a veterinarian.
ateChocolate.steps[3].title: Step 4: Go to Vet for Cardiac Monitoring
ateChocolate.steps[3].content: Your vet may recommend induced vomiting (if early), activated charcoal, and ECG monitoring to watch for arrhythmias.
ateChocolate.faqs[0].question: Is chocolate toxic to cats?
ateChocolate.faqs[0].answer: Yes, chocolate is toxic to cats — often more so than to dogs relative to body weight. Cats are more sensitive to theobromine because they metabolize it more slowly. The same toxic principle applies: theobromine and caffeine cause CNS stimulation, cardiac arrhythmias, and potentially seizures.
ateChocolate.faqs[1].question: Why are cats more sensitive than dogs?
ateChocolate.faqs[1].answer: Cats have lower activity of cytochrome P450 enzymes responsible for metabolizing theobromine. While dogs take 17+ hours to clear theobromine, cats may take even longer. Additionally, cats typically weigh less (4-6kg average), so the dose-per-kg ratio from the same amount of chocolate is higher.
ateChocolate.faqs[2].question: How much chocolate is toxic to cats?
ateChocolate.faqs[2].answer: Milk chocolate becomes toxic at approximately 0.5 oz per pound of body weight. Dark chocolate and baking chocolate are 2-5x more toxic. For a 5kg (11lb) cat, as little as 20g of milk chocolate (about half a standard bar) can cause symptoms. Baking chocolate is lethal at 5-10g for an average cat.
ateChocolate.faqs[3].question: What should I do if my cat ate chocolate?
ateChocolate.faqs[3].answer: Call ASPCA Poison Control at (888) 426-4435 or your vet immediately. Cats are more sensitive than dogs — even small amounts are concerning. Bring the chocolate packaging to identify theobromine content. Do NOT wait for symptoms, as cardiac arrhythmias can be sudden and fatal.

ateOnion.steps[0].title: Step 1: Note the Type and Amount
ateOnion.steps[0].content: Was it raw onion, cooked onion, onion powder, or a product containing onion? Powder is most concentrated. Calculate approximate amount.
ateOnion.steps[1].title: Step 2: Call Vet or Poison Control
ateOnion.steps[1].content: 📞 ASPCA Poison Control: (888) 426-4435. Even small amounts can cause delayed anemia — early blood work may be needed.
ateOnion.steps[2].title: Step 3: Do NOT Induce Vomiting Unless Instructed
ateOnion.steps[2].content: ⚠️ Symptoms are delayed 1-5 days. Induction is not effective after absorption. Your vet may induce vomiting if ingestion was very recent.
ateOnion.steps[3].title: Step 4: Schedule Blood Work
ateOnion.steps[3].content: Your vet will check for Heinz bodies and monitor red blood cell count for 3-5 days. Early detection of anemia allows transfusion if needed.
ateOnion.faqs[0].question: Are onions toxic to cats?
ateOnion.faqs[0].answer: Yes, onions are highly toxic to cats — more so than dogs relative to body weight. Onions contain N-propyl disulfide and thiosulfates that cause oxidative damage to red blood cells, leading to Heinz body hemolytic anemia. Cats are uniquely vulnerable because their hemoglobin is more susceptible to oxidation, and they produce methemoglobin more readily.
ateOnion.faqs[1].question: How much onion is toxic to cats?
ateOnion.faqs[1].answer: Even small amounts are dangerous. Toxic effects can occur at 5g/kg body weight (about 1 tablespoon for a 4kg cat). Regular consumption of smaller amounts (even trace amounts in baby food or broth) can cause cumulative damage. Raw, cooked, powdered, and dehydrated onions are all toxic.
ateOnion.faqs[2].question: What are the symptoms of onion poisoning in cats?
ateOnion.faqs[2].answer: Symptoms appear 1-5 days after ingestion: pale or yellow gums (anemia/jaundice), weakness, rapid breathing, reddish-brown urine (hemoglobinuria), vomiting, and lethargy. Heinz body anemia is confirmed by blood smear showing damaged red blood cells. Severe cases require blood transfusion.
ateOnion.faqs[3].question: Can onion powder hurt cats?
ateOnion.faqs[3].answer: Yes, onion powder is concentrated and especially dangerous. Even small amounts in broth, gravy, baby food, or treats can cause toxicity. Many commercial products contain hidden onion or garlic powder. Always check ingredient labels before sharing human food with cats.

ateGarlic.steps[0].title: Step 1: Remove All Garlic Immediately
ateGarlic.steps[0].content: Remove any remaining garlic, garlic-containing foods, or supplements from your cat's reach.
ateGarlic.steps[1].title: Step 2: Call Poison Control
ateGarlic.steps[1].content: 📞 ASPCA Poison Control: (888) 426-4435. Garlic is more toxic than onion — small amounts require professional guidance.
ateGarlic.steps[2].title: Step 3: Schedule Blood Work for Days 3-5
ateGarlic.steps[2].content: Anemia peaks 3-5 days after ingestion. Even if your cat seems fine, delayed Heinz body anemia can be life-threatening.
ateGarlic.faqs[0].question: Is garlic toxic to cats?
ateGarlic.faqs[0].answer: Yes, garlic is highly toxic to cats — approximately 5x more potent than onion per gram. Garlic (Allium sativum) contains allicin, alliin, and allyl propyl disulfide, which cause severe oxidative damage to feline red blood cells. Cats are uniquely susceptible due to the structure of their hemoglobin molecule.
ateGarlic.faqs[1].question: How much garlic is toxic to cats?
ateGarlic.faqs[1].answer: As little as 5g of garlic per kg of body weight can cause toxicity. For a 4kg cat, this equals just 1 small clove (approximately 5g). Toxic effects can also occur from chronic low-dose exposure — even trace amounts in food or supplements over weeks can accumulate and cause anemia.
ateGarlic.faqs[2].question: Is garlic salt/powder dangerous for cats?
ateGarlic.faqs[2].answer: Yes, garlic powder and salt are concentrated forms. As little as 1/8 teaspoon of garlic powder can be toxic to a small cat. Dry garlic powder, garlic supplements, garlic-flavored treats, and garlic-infused oils all pose risks. Many human foods contain hidden garlic — always check labels.
ateGarlic.faqs[3].question: What are the symptoms of garlic poisoning in cats?
ateGarlic.faqs[3].answer: Symptoms develop 1-5 days after ingestion: pale gums (anemia), lethargy, weakness, rapid breathing, elevated heart rate, jaundice (yellow gums/eyes), reddish-brown urine, vomiting, and collapse. Heinz body anemia is confirmed by blood smear. Severe cases require blood transfusions.

ateEssentialOils.steps[0].title: Step 1: Wash Your Cat If Oil Is On Fur/Skin
ateEssentialOils.steps[0].content: Use Dawn dish soap (cuts oil) to wash off any topical exposure. Rinse thoroughly. Do NOT use water alone — oil repels water.
ateEssentialOils.steps[1].title: Step 2: Remove From Exposure Source
ateEssentialOils.steps[1].content: Turn off diffusers, remove oil containers, and ventilate the area. Move your cat to fresh air.
ateEssentialOils.steps[2].title: Step 3: Call Poison Control
ateEssentialOils.steps[2].content: 📞 ASPCA Poison Control: (888) 426-4435. Bring the oil bottle — tell them the botanical name and phenol/terpene content if listed.
ateEssentialOils.steps[3].title: Step 4: Do NOT Induce Vomiting
ateEssentialOils.steps[3].content: ⚠️ Essential oils have high aspiration pneumonia risk. Vomiting can cause oil to enter lungs. Go to vet for safe decontamination.
ateEssentialOils.faqs[0].question: Why are essential oils toxic to cats?
ateEssentialOils.faqs[0].answer: Cats lack UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT) enzymes needed to metabolize certain compounds in essential oils (terpenes, phenols, ketones). This makes them 10x more sensitive than dogs to tea tree oil, citrus oils, eucalyptus, peppermint, and pine oils. Even topical application on skin can cause toxicity if the cat licks it off.
ateEssentialOils.faqs[1].question: Which essential oils are most dangerous for cats?
ateEssentialOils.faqs[1].answer: Most dangerous: Tea tree (melaleuca), wintergreen, peppermint, pine, eucalyptus, citrus (limonene, linalool), cinnamon, clove, ylang ylang, birch, and thyme. Tea tree oil is most commonly reported — even 10-20mL on skin can be fatal. Diffusers are also dangerous as cats inhale droplets and groom them from fur.
ateEssentialOils.faqs[2].question: What are the symptoms of essential oil poisoning in cats?
ateEssentialOils.faqs[2].answer: Symptoms depend on oil type and route: (1) Ingestion: drooling, vomiting, tremors, ataxia, weakness, hypothermia. (2) Skin absorption: lethargy, hypersalivation, liver damage. (3) Inhalation: respiratory distress, aspiration pneumonia. Tea tree oil specifically causes severe hypothermia and ataxia within 2-8 hours.
ateEssentialOils.faqs[3].question: Are essential oil diffusers dangerous for cats?
ateEssentialOils.faqs[3].answer: Yes, diffusers pose three risks: (1) Inhaled droplets settle on fur and are groomed off, causing ingestion. (2) Volatilized oils irritate feline respiratory passages (cats have efficient smell but sensitive airways). (3) Concentrated oil in the diffuser water can be spilled and licked. Use diffusers only in well-ventilated rooms your cat cannot access.

ateFishingLine.criticalWarning.lines[0]: NEVER pull on string protruding from your cat. The line may be anchored internally — pulling can cut through the intestine.
ateFishingLine.criticalWarning.lines[1]: ALWAYS check under your cat's tongue. Fishing line frequently anchors at the base of the tongue.
ateFishingLine.criticalWarning.lines[2]: This requires emergency surgery — do not wait for symptoms.
ateFishingLine.riskAssessment.rows[0].ac: 🚨 DO NOT PULL — Emergency vet NOW
ateFishingLine.steps[0].title: Step 1: Check Under Your Cat's Tongue
ateFishingLine.steps[0].content: Gently open your mouth and look under the tongue and at the base. Fishing line commonly anchors here. If you see string — do NOT pull.
ateFishingLine.steps[1].title: Step 2: Do NOT Pull Any Protruding String
ateFishingLine.steps[1].content: ⚠️ Pulling can cause the line to saw through the intestinal wall. Leave it alone and go to emergency vet.
ateFishingLine.steps[2].title: Step 3: Go to Emergency Vet for X-rays/Surgery
ateFishingLine.steps[2].content: Linear foreign bodies often require surgical removal. Your vet will take X-rays, start IV fluids, and perform enterotomy to remove the line.
ateFishingLine.steps[3].title: Step 4: Prepare for Hospitalization
ateFishingLine.steps[3].content: Post-surgery, your cat will need 2-5 days hospitalization for IV antibiotics, pain management, and monitoring for anastomotic leakage.
ateFishingLine.faqs[0].question: Why is fishing line so dangerous for cats?
ateFishingLine.faqs[0].answer: Fishing line is a linear foreign body — when swallowed, it anchors at one end (under tongue, in stomach, or at pylorus) while the rest extends through the intestines. Peristalsis pulls the line taut, causing the intestine to accordion-pleat around it. The line then saws through the intestinal wall, causing multiple perforations, peritonitis, and death if not surgically removed.
ateFishingLine.faqs[1].question: What are the symptoms of linear foreign body in cats?
ateFishingLine.faqs[1].answer: Symptoms include: string visible under tongue or protruding from anus, vomiting (especially after eating), drooling, difficulty swallowing, loss of appetite, abdominal pain, lethargy, and fever. CRITICAL: Always check under the tongue and around the base of the tongue — the line may be anchored there.
ateFishingLine.faqs[2].question: Should I pull the string out of my cat?
ateFishingLine.faqs[2].answer: NO! Never pull on a string or line protruding from your cat mouth or anus. The line may be anchored internally — pulling it can saw through the intestinal wall causing perforations. Go to emergency vet immediately for proper removal under anesthesia.
ateFishingLine.faqs[3].question: What is the treatment for fishing line ingestion in cats?
ateFishingLine.faqs[3].answer: Treatment requires emergency surgery (enterotomy or gastrotomy) to remove the line. Multiple incisions may be needed along the intestine to release the plicated segments. IV antibiotics treat peritonitis, and fluids correct dehydration. Prognosis depends on how many perforations occurred — early surgery has 80-90% survival; delayed treatment with multiple perforations has 50-60% survival.

ateLily.steps[0].title: Step 1: EMERGENCY VET NOW
ateLily.steps[0].content: Go to the nearest emergency vet immediately. Call ASPCA Poison Control at (888) 426-4435 en route. Time is critical.
ateLily.steps[1].title: Step 2: Bring a Plant Sample
ateLily.steps[1].content: Take the lily plant or a photo to the vet. This confirms the species and helps assess toxicity risk.
ateLily.steps[2].title: Step 3: IV Fluids Are Critical
ateLily.steps[2].content: Your vet will start aggressive IV fluid therapy to protect the kidneys. This must begin within 18 hours of ingestion for best outcomes.
ateLily.steps[3].title: Step 4: Activated Charcoal May Help
ateLily.steps[3].content: If ingestion was recent, your vet may administer activated charcoal to absorb remaining toxins in the GI tract.
ateLily.faqs[0].question: Which lilies are toxic to cats?
ateLily.faqs[0].answer: True lilies (Lilium spp.) and Hemerocallis (daylilies) are highly toxic: Easter lily, Tiger lily, Asiatic lily, Oriental lily, Stargazer lily. Even pollen, leaves, or water from the vase can cause kidney failure. Not toxic: Peace lily, Lily of the Valley (different toxin), Calla lily.
ateLily.faqs[1].question: How much lily is toxic to cats?
ateLily.faqs[1].answer: Ingestion of as little as 2-3 petals or leaves, or exposure to pollen (grooming pollen off fur), can cause acute kidney failure. There is no safe amount — any exposure requires emergency veterinary treatment.
ateLily.faqs[2].question: How long after lily ingestion do symptoms appear?
ateLily.faqs[2].answer: Vomiting and lethargy begin within 1-6 hours. Kidney damage is detectable within 12-24 hours. Without treatment, kidney failure develops within 24-72 hours and is often fatal. Early IV fluid therapy is critical.

ateString.steps[0].title: Step 1: Call Your Vet Immediately
ateString.steps[0].content: Contact your veterinarian right away. Note when the string was eaten and how much.
ateString.steps[1].title: Step 2: DO NOT Pull Visible String
ateString.steps[1].content: If string is hanging from the mouth or anus, do NOT pull it. This can cause the anchored end to cut through intestinal tissue.
ateString.steps[2].title: Step 3: Check Under the Tongue
ateString.steps[2].content: If safe to do so, check if string is wrapped around the base of the tongue. If so, this is an emergency — go to the vet NOW.
ateString.steps[3].title: Step 4: Monitor for Symptoms
ateString.steps[3].content: Watch for vomiting, loss of appetite, lethargy, drooling, and inability to defecate. These require emergency surgery.
ateString.faqs[0].question: Why is string dangerous for cats?
ateString.faqs[0].answer: String is a "linear foreign body" — it anchors at the base of the tongue or stomach and the rest is pulled through the intestines as they contract. This causes the intestines to "pleat" (bunch up) and the string can cut through the intestinal wall like a wire, causing perforation, peritonitis, and death.
ateString.faqs[1].question: What are the symptoms of string ingestion?
ateString.faqs[1].answer: Vomiting, loss of appetite, lethargy, drooling, visible string hanging from the mouth or anus, abdominal pain, and inability to defecate. If you see string, DO NOT pull it — this can cause more damage.
ateString.faqs[2].question: How is string ingestion treated?
ateString.faqs[2].answer: Treatment depends on location. If the string is still in the mouth/tongue, your vet may cut it. If it has entered the GI tract, surgery is often required to remove it safely. X-rays and ultrasound help determine the best approach.
